source_text: Paulus servus Jesu Christi. Requiramus cur servus dicatur is qui alibi scribit: Non enim accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis. Cum liber sim ab omnibus, omnibus me servum feci. Servit ergo Christo non in spiritu servitutis sed in spiritu adoptionis, quia omni libertate nobilior est servitus Christi. Gloria Christo. Amen.
thought_title: Paul's service to Christ as adoption, not slavery
orientation: Origen has just announced he will begin explaining Romans, and now he takes up Paul's opening self-description, 'Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ,' asking why Paul calls himself a servant.
pass_a_gloss: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ. Let us ask why he is called a servant, the one who writes elsewhere: For you have not received the spirit of slavery again in fear, but you have received the spirit of adoption. Though I am free from all, I have made myself a servant to all. Therefore he serves Christ not in the spirit of slavery but in the spirit of adoption, because the service of Christ is nobler than every freedom. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary does not ban 'servant' for servus, and it preserves the social metaphor Paul uses for his relation to Christ.
Literal rendering keeps the contrast with 'the spirit of adoption' and matches the Vetus Latina wording Paul quotes.
The glossary defines adoptio as adoption, and this exact phrase is the fixed term for the Spirit's work.
rejected: the spirit of being God's children

choices.why: Keeps the comparative force of the Latin and the rhetorical point that Christ's service surpasses freedom.
A doxological formula; literal rendering preserves its liturgical force.

pass_b_english: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ. Let us ask why the man who writes elsewhere, “For you did not receive the spirit of slavery again in fear, but you received the spirit of adoption” (Romans 8:15), calls himself a servant. “Though I am free from all, I made myself a servant to all” (1 Corinthians 9:19). So he serves Christ not in the spirit of slavery but in the spirit of adoption, because Christ's service is nobler than every freedom. Glory to Christ. Amen.
